title: Remap CapsLock to Ctrl does not work in Hyper-V Windows 11 VM

judgment.rationale: The report has a concrete Hyper-V guest remap failure, but the session/input mode and where PowerToys runs are not established. Related issue #21416 closed, but that closure does not show this report was fixed.
evidence: The issue says a CapsLock-to-Ctrl remap does not work in a Windows 11 Hyper-V VM.
The thread links the related issue #21416, which is now closed.
No current-build retest, VMConnect session mode, or confirmed workaround is documented.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce in a controlled Hyper-V guest with host/guest PowerToys state and session mode recorded; do not treat #21416's closure as resolution evidence.

fix_assessment.rationale: The host-versus-guest configuration and input session mode are missing, and the related issue closure provides no evidence that this case is fixed.

issue_context.summary: A CapsLock-to-Ctrl remap reportedly fails in a Windows 11 Hyper-V VM; the available thread does not distinguish host interception from guest-side remapping or session transport.
known_information: The issue is labeled Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, and Product-Keyboard Manager.
The reported destination is Ctrl and the failing target is a Windows 11 Hyper-V guest.
The issue references #21416, which is closed but does not provide proof of a fix for this report.
inferences: The remap may be applied on the host while the VM session captures or translates the key first, or the guest may have its own PowerToys configuration.
Enhanced-session versus basic-session input could change which keyboard events reach the remapper.
issue_context.analysis: Use a small controlled Hyper-V test and identify which OS instance runs Keyboard Manager. The old related issue should not be used as a handled status without a linked fix or a current confirmation.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and both comments.
Checked the related #21416 status; it is closed, but no evidence links its closure to a resolution of #34549.

reproduce.title: Test CapsLock-to-Ctrl remapping across Hyper-V session modes
prerequisites: A Windows 11 Hyper-V host and disposable Windows 11 guest.
Keyboard Manager installed on the host and a clean test configuration.
steps: Verify the CapsLock-to-Ctrl mapping works on the host outside the VM.
With the remap configured on the host, test the guest in the current VMConnect session mode and record whether it receives Ctrl.
Repeat in the alternate available VMConnect mode, such as Enhanced Session versus basic session.
If PowerToys is also installed in the guest, disable one instance at a time and compare.
reproduce.expected_result: The configuration identifies the point where CapsLock is translated or captured, and the remap works in the supported host/guest input path.
